I’m afraid I don’t have real‑time access to external databases or APIs, so I can’t pull a definitive “official” calendar straight out of a government source right now.  
However, I can give you a fairly complete overview of the **long‑weekend** dates that Canadians enjoyed during 2023 based on the federal statutory holidays and how most employers observed them across the country.  

---

### 🇨🇦 Canada – Typical Long Weekends in 2023

| Date | Holiday | Observed By | Why It’s a Long Weekend |
|------|---------|-------------|------------------------|
| **Jan 2** | *New Year’s Day* (observed) | Most workplaces & schools | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday → many offices closed Monday, giving a four‑day break. |
| **Feb 20** | *Family Day* (Alberta, BC, NB, ON, SK) | Those provinces | Falls on Thursday → many people take Friday off. |
| **Mar 31** | *Good Friday* | All provinces | Friday itself + Saturday gives a three‑day weekend. |
| **Apr 9** | *Easter Monday* (Ontario, PEI, NL, Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Yukon) | These regions | Adds a day after Easter Sunday, creating a five‑day stretch for residents who work outside the region. |
| **May 22** | *Victoria Day* | All provinces | Monday before May 23 → classic spring long weekend. |
| **Jul 1** | *Canada Day* | All provinces | Tuesday → often combined with the preceding Monday (July 3) for a four‑day break. |
| **Sep 8** | *Labour Day* | All provinces | Monday → standard one‑day long weekend. |
| **Oct 10** | *Thanksgiving* | All provinces | Monday → another single‑day long weekend. |
| **Nov 11** | *Remembrance Day* | Some provinces (BC, AB, MB, NS, PEI, NL, NT, YT) | Thursday → many workers take Friday off. |
| **Dec 24–27** | *Christmas & Boxing Day* | All provinces | Christmas Eve (Sunday) + Christmas Day (Monday) + Boxing Day (Tuesday) → many people enjoy a four‑to‑five‑day break depending on their employer's policy. |

> **Note:**  
> • Provincial variations exist—e.g., *St. Patrick’s Day* (March 17) is a statutory holiday only in Newfoundland & Labrador, while *Civic Holiday* (first Monday in August) applies mainly in Ontario and Manitoba.  
> • Employers may offer additional paid leave around other holidays such as *National Indigenous Peoples Day* (June 21) or *Labrador Day* (August 15).

---

#### How You Can Verify / Pull Official Data Yourself

If your holiday‑planning app needs authoritative data:

1. **Government Websites**  
   - `https://www.canada.ca/en/services/publications.html` – contains links to provincial labour standards pages listing statutory holidays.  
   - Each province’s Ministry of Finance or Employment department usually publishes a PDF calendar for the fiscal year.

2. **Open Government Data Portals**  
   - Many provinces host datasets under open licenses (e.g., Alberta’s `data.alberta.ca`, British Columbia’s `open.gov.bc.ca`). Search for “statutory holidays 2023”.

3. **API Options**  
   - While not all governments expose RESTful endpoints, services like [Calendarific](https://calendarific.com/) provide holiday calendars for free tiers.  
   - Example request:  
     ```
     GET https://calendarific.com/api/v2/holidays?api_key=YOUR_KEY&country=CA&year=2023
     ```

4. **Scraping** *(if permitted)*  
   - If the site offers a static HTML table, simple scraping scripts (Python BeautifulSoup, Node.js Cheerio) will extract the dates.

5. **Local Libraries**  
   - For historical accuracy, consult local libraries’ digital archives—they often keep printed copies of annual holiday notices.

---

Let me know if you'd like help writing code snippets to retrieve this data programmatically, or if there's anything else I can clarify!
